title: Segmented per-route prefetch governor with tiered allowlist controls and safe rollback
creator: Priya Shah
description: Problem: Hosts show wide variance in per-tenant token cost and tail latency due to a one-size-fits-all batching and KV prefetch configuration. Some high-throughput routes can afford larger batch windows and aggressive KV prefetching; others (stateful or privacy-sensitive) must avoid caching or batching entirely. We need an automated, per-customer and per-route governor that: (1) classifies routes into segments, (2) generates batching/caching recommendations per segment and per customer tier, (3) enforces allowlists/denylists for routes that should not be batched or cached, and (4) applies changes with safe dry-run/canary/apply/automatic-rollback if SLOs regress.
acceptance_criteria: A ruleset engine exists that returns per-route configuration (batch_window_ms, max_batch_size, kv_prefetch: true|false, cache_ttl_ms) for a given tenant and route
Console UI surfaces automated recommendations and a one-click dry-run for a single customer
Canary deployment path applies config to <1% traffic and auto-rolls back if p99 latency or error-rate thresholds are exceeded
Allowlist/denylist support plumbs from Console to runtime and prevents caching/batching for marked routes
Audit logs capture each generated recommendation, who approved it, and exact diffs applied
Automated cost telemetry shows improvement per-tenant after applying recommendations in a 2-week canary
implementation_steps: Design ruleset schema: segmentation keys (route_pattern, tenant_tier, qps_bucket, stateful_flag) and output knobs (batch_window_ms, max_batch_size, kv_prefetch, cache_ttl_ms)
Build offline recommender that analyzes 30d traffic by route+tenant and proposes knobs; store proposals in /internal/cost-proposals
Implement ruleset evaluation in runtime that resolves customer+route -> effective knobs with deterministic tie-breakers
Add allowlist/denylist enforcement path: runtime consults a fast ACL cache for routes excluded from batching/caching
Implement dry-run mode where runtime logs what would change but does not alter behaviour; export diffs to observability
Integrate canary controller: progressive traffic ramp, SLO guards, auto-rollback hooks tied to alerting rules
Console integration: recommendations tab, approve/dismiss workflow, manual apply and schedule
End-to-end tests and canary in staging cluster, then small customer pilot
testing_plan: Unit tests for ruleset merge logic and tie-breakers
Deterministic replay of 7d traffic in staging to verify recommendations match offline expectations
Load test with synthetic tenants for gold/silver/bronze tiers to validate cost/latency tradeoffs
Chaos test: simulate KV eviction and confirm allowlist routes behave correctly (no caching)
Regression test: ensure existing per-route SLAs are never violated during dry-run
Post-apply A/B: measure cost-per-token and p50/p95/p99 latency for affected traffic segments
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (dry-run): run recommender and record diffs for 2 weeks; surface in Console
Phase 1 (canary): apply to 0.5% of traffic for 48 hours with strict SLO gates
Phase 2 (graduated): after canary success, expand to 5% for 7 days, monitor cost and latency
Phase 3 (tiered rollout): enable per-tier defaults (gold conservative, silver balanced, bronze aggressive) and allow tenant opt-out
Phase 4 (full): bulk apply for low-risk segments and provide rollback window of 72 hours
monitoring_and_metrics: Cost metrics: cost_per_1k_tokens by tenant and route
Performance SLOs: p50/p95/p99 generation latency and tail error rate
Operational: KV cache hit rate, average batch size, batching delay (ms), QPS
Safety triggers: >10% relative p99 increase OR >0.5% absolute increase in error rate => auto-rollback
Audit: config-change events with proposer, approver, timestamp, and diff
